content.text:
I accepted the challenge in full and saved the revised `finding.json` with `accepted: true`. The challenger's queries backed up every point, so I didn't need new queries to push back on any of them.

**What changed in F6:**
- **Narrower claim.** Equipment is now the core of the finding. After an equipment short line, the same customer gets the same SKU within 10 days only 1.03% of the time, against 2.50% after a stock line in the same year and month (q335). At 63 days it is still lower: 8.69% vs 9.28% (q352). Against the lines' own buying beforehand, equipment shows no recovery either (q304).
- **Withdrawn claim.** I dropped "only a small slice comes back" for parts, refrigeration and supplies. Within 63 days, 35.7%–40.2% of their short lines are followed by a shipped re-order, against 23.7%–26.0% after stock lines (q352).
- **Lower size.** On short lines, the recorded price ignores the line's markdown (q348). With markdown applied and duplicate retries removed, the headline drops to 1,863,423.16 a year for 2017–2024, of which equipment is 1,346,950.19 (q350). It was 2,165,946.53. Repricing at same-year stock prices gives almost the same figure (q342). The 2024 figure falls from 1,886,231.28 to 1,036,894.61.
- **2025 is no longer excluded.** It is a full year, and I now report it separately at 2,233,380.86 (q350). The rise is concentrated in R-454B equipment, where 4,852 of 17,130 lines were short (q319). I kept the 2017–2024 average as the headline because 2025 looks like a refrigerant changeover, not a steady rate.
- **What held up.** Short lines are real unfilled lines that were never invoiced (q294, q296). They are not linked to discontinued products (q307). The seasonal drop explains most of the dip in customers' equipment buying afterwards, but not all of it (q335).

Confidence stays medium. The equipment pattern holds across every test, but the dollar figure is an upper bound at standard cost. The data still can't say whether unrecovered demand went to a competitor, was postponed, or was cancelled.
